chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi that he was asked about a man whose death approaches and he divorces his wife, is his divorce valid? He said:

Yes, and if he dies she inherits him, and if she dies he does not inherit her. This does not contradict the earlier reports, because the way to reconcile them is to understand the earlier reports as meaning that he does not have the right to divorce her with a divorce that severs the inheritance between them. For divorce is of two types: revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in). In all cases, inheritance remains between them if it occurs during the illness, as long as she has not exited the waiting period ('iddah). Once she exits the waiting period, the wife inherits him for as long as there is between them and one year, provided she has not married. If she marries, her inheritance from him is cut off. And if she does not marry, she inherits him until one year. If the year passes completely, her inheritance from him is also nullified.
ai.seo_question: Does a deathbed divorce sever the wife's right to inherit from her husband?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between reports by distinguishing between revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorces, clarifying that inheritance persists as long as the wife remains in her waiting period (iddah) or within one year if she does not remarry. This ruling ensures that a deathbed divorce does not unfairly disinherit the spouse, maintaining the financial rights established during the marital bond until the iddah concludes or the one-year limit expires.
